PullRequest.Title: chat: add telemetry for collapsible content toggles
PullRequest.Body:
- Add `chat.collapsibleToggle` to the shared chat collapsible component so user expand/collapse clicks are tracked across thinking, terminal, references, subagent, hook, markdown, auto-mode, and question-answer blocks.
- Record the collapsible `kind`, its previous expanded state, the configured thinking style, and whether a terminal block is rendered inside thinking.
- Keep `terminal/chatThinkingBlockToggle` for terminal-specific analysis while assigning the shared event to `justschen` and the terminal event to `anthonykim1`.
- Exclude programmatic and automatic expansion, as well as rows explicitly marked non-expandable.
- Add unit coverage for thinking and terminal header toggles.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The shared user-gesture entry point comes from [`ChatCollapsibleContentPart.toggleExpanded`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/06c80b32d80434459b780fbca380dd99f7d76feb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatCollapsibleContentPart.ts#L168-L175).
- The terminal event shape and `previousExpanded` property follow [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart.toggleOutputFromAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/06c80b32d80434459b780fbca380dd99f7d76feb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L1223-L1238).
- The `thinkingStyle` property follows [`ChatThinkingStyleUsageEvent`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/06c80b32d80434459b780fbca380dd99f7d76feb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts#L264-L276).

Scenarios.Scenario: User expands or collapses a thinking, references, markdown, hook, subagent, auto-mode, or question-answer block.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The button click synchronously calls toggleExpanded, reads the in-memory thinking-style configuration, logs one telemetry event, then dispatches the existing DOM event and updates expansion state. Telemetry cleaning/appender enqueueing is on the click path, but remote delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one chat.collapsibleToggle event through ITelemetryService; desktop enqueues one shared-process IPC call and web hands one event to the telemetry appender/SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one telemetry submission per explicit expandable-header click; no collection loop, rendering fan-out, or retry is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The click directly dispatched the user-toggle DOM event and changed the observable expansion state, with no telemetry boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration lookup, small-object cleaning/copying, and appender enqueue occur synchronously before expansion changes; actual IPC/network completion is asynchronous and does not block the toggle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales linearly with explicit user clicks, not message count or streaming updates; each click carries four scalar fields.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Clicks are handled serially by the UI event loop. The change adds no queue, worker, promise fan-out, or concurrent requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The configuration read uses the already-loaded in-memory configuration model. Telemetry may temporarily buffer events until experiment properties are available, but that existing buffer is capped at 1000; there is no new cache key or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added call is directly on the click handler path, and telemetry implementation shows synchronous cleaning followed by asynchronous IPC/SDK enqueueing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender implementation differs between desktop and web, but the introduced cardinality is fixed at one event per deliberate click and payload size is constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded constant work to a low-frequency user gesture, with no realistic multiplicative trigger or blocked remote boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: User expands or collapses a terminal command block rendered in the thinking container.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The terminal wrapper uses the same click path, but logUserToggle submits the shared event and then a terminal-specific event before the existing expansion-state update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit chat.collapsibleToggle and terminal/chatThinkingBlockToggle through ITelemetryService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two telemetry submissions per explicit terminal-header click, each with a constant four- or three-field payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This wrapper's header click changed expansion state without these two telemetry submissions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both events are cleaned and enqueued synchronously, but IPC/network completion is not awaited; the fixed work precedes the visual state update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales as two fixed submissions per deliberate terminal toggle, independent of command output size, terminal history, and number of blocks in the response.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two submissions are sequential on one click; separate clicks remain serialized by the UI event loop, and no burst concurrency is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same in-memory configuration lookup and bounded telemetry startup buffer apply. No output content is serialized into telemetry and no per-terminal cache is created.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the kind override deterministically selects the second call, and the test asserts exactly two events per click.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact enqueue cost varies by platform and enabled appenders, but output size and chat history cannot amplify the payload or call count for one gesture.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Two fixed telemetry enqueues on an infrequent explicit gesture do not establish meaningful latency, throughput, or network degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat responses render, stream, and automatically change collapsible expansion state without a user click.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Constructors now receive the shared telemetry service, but rendering and setExpanded-driven automatic changes do not call logUserToggle. Content lazy initialization and existing DOM/layout work remain unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response block count controls the number of constructor references passed, but not telemetry calls; streaming/programmatic state transitions use setExpanded rather than toggleExpanded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work, IPC burst, or per-block telemetry fan-out occurs during render or streaming.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ITelemetryService is a delayed singleton, so all parts retain only the same service reference. The surrounding chat surface already injects that service, and no per-part telemetry cache or listener is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed logging call is reachable only from toggleExpanded, whose base registration and additional thinking call sites are click listeners; automatic paths call setExpanded directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism: constructor injection itself does not perform per-block logging or allocate a service per instance.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Rendering many blocks adds only a shared service reference per existing object and does not introduce expensive boundaries or repeated telemetry work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and traced the shared and terminal toggle paths through configuration lookup, telemetry cleaning, appenders, IPC/network enqueueing, automatic expansion, and service lifecycle. The new work is bounded to one or two constant-size telemetry submissions per explicit user click; no high-confidence performance regression or regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
